item.title: Late exam papers put remote schools at risk
item.description: Manalos Aviation is urging the National Department of Education to deliver Grade 8 examination papers earlier after completing deliveries to 199 schools across Morobe Province under a tight schedule. Chief Executive Officer Captain Jurgen Ruh said the papers arrived later than in previous years, leaving limited time to reach remote schools before examinations began on Monday, October 19.
item.content:encoded:
Manalos Aviation is urging the National Department of Education to deliver Grade 8 examination papers earlier after completing deliveries to 199 schools across Morobe Province under a tight schedule.

Chief Executive Officer Captain Jurgen Ruh said the papers arrived later than in previous years, leaving limited time to reach remote schools before examinations began on Monday, October 19.

“The papers came very late. I think this year they came even a day later than last year,” Captain Ruh said.

Manalos Aviation completed deliveries late Sunday evening, covering 128 locations across the province. Its BK117 helicopter landed at 42 locations, while a police helicopter reached 86 locations. Some schools received examination papers through bulk drop-offs for further distribution.

Ruh said Manalos Aviation had delivered examination papers in Morobe for 17 years, but the late arrival of materials continued to put pressure on the operation.

The teams completed the deliveries after two consecutive days of favourable weather, working from 7am to 5pm.

“We were lucky that we had two days of great weather, which you can't bank on,” Ruh said.

He said bad weather or aircraft problems could have delayed deliveries, particularly to schools in remote areas with limited road access.

Ruh is calling on the department to provide examination papers and confirmed school lists at least 10 days before examinations begin.

He said earlier delivery would give aviation crews enough time to plan flight routes, account for changes to school lists and schedule operations around weather conditions.

“Just bring us the exam papers early enough, please. Just bring them earlier,” he said.

Ruh said timely delivery was critical to ensuring students in remote communities received their examination papers and could sit their examinations alongside other students across the province.

Manalos Aviation will also assist with collecting completed examination papers for marking, with materials from some areas consolidated at collection points before being transported.

Ruh said improved logistics planning was needed to reduce pressure on aviation crews and ensure examination papers reached remote schools well before examinations began.

item.title: Wau Waria prepares ahead of El Nino funding
item.description: The Wau Waria District in the Morobe Province has already established a dedicated El Niño Response Committee, which will be responsible for the delivery of relief assistance when funding is made available. Wau Waria MP, Marsh Narewec, said this in a statement when giving an update on the district’s preparedness, as well as the National Government’s promised allocation of K2.5 million.
item.content:encoded:
The Wau Waria District in the Morobe Province has already established a dedicated El Niño Response Committee, which will be responsible for the delivery of relief assistance when funding is made available.

Wau Waria MP, Marsh Narewec, said this in a statement when giving an update on the district’s preparedness, as well as the National Government’s promised allocation of K2.5 million.

Mr Narewec said that the district has not received its share of funding as yet, because these monies were deposited into the National Banking Corporation [NBC] for the first time, and this is something his district officers need to understand and comply with before accessing these funds.

He said that the district under the leadership of the Chief Executive Officer, John Orebut, has put in a working committee structure, who will immediately be able to assist communities, as soon as the funds are formally released by the bank.

"Like other districts in Morobe Province, Wau Waria is working through these new requirements, with a workshop scheduled for this week, to guide our finance officers through the necessary banking procedures, financial processes and requirements to help speed up the process of accessing the funds, Mr Narewec said."

Mr Narewec said that the District Management Team [DMT], led by Mr Orebut, had convened meetings to review drought damage reports, identify priority needs, and develop a proposed response work plan and budget, from October 13 th to the 15 th .

"To our people doing it tough in this dry spell, we hear you and we are working hard to get help to those who need it most at the earliest," Narewec said.

He also said that district has also established a separate oversight body, comprising of LLG Managers, Programme Managers, government officers, business houses, churches and community representatives, to reflect Mr. Narewec's strong emphasis on transparency and accountability.

Mr Narewec said that this will ensure decisions on disaster relief are not left solely to the district administration, but are subjected to broader consultation, scrutiny and endorsement.

The Committee met on Tuesday October 20th to finalize the plan, budget, and how help will be delivered, and have since deployed three teams across the district's three LLGs of Wau Urban, Wau Rural and Waria, to conduct awareness and collect firsthand information on the extent of drought-related hardships affecting individual communities.

Mr. Narewec also added that the district will deploy the KoboToolBox, which is a digital data collection platform, which will systematically gather drought impact information from individual wards.

He further added that this is done so they assist the most affected wards and do not rely on a blanket approach, because of the level of support and funding they currently have.

item.title: Mobiha acting PPL CEO
item.description: PNG Power Ltd Board has announced the appointment of Noel Mobiha as its new Acting Chief Executive Officer following the resignation of Paul Bayly, effective as of Tuesday 20th October. Mobiha will oversee PPL's operations for an interim period until a permanent CEO is appointed.
item.content:encoded:
PNG Power Ltd Board has announced the appointment of Noel Mobiha as its new Acting Chief Executive Officer following the resignation of Paul Bayly, effective as of Tuesday 20th October.

Mobiha will oversee PPL's operations for an interim period until a permanent CEO is appointed.

Mr. Bayly's resignation comes at a crucial time as the company continues to navigate ongoing operational challenges.

PPL Board Chairman, Malcolm Lewis has confirmed that in an internal circular, the board accepted Mr. Bayly's resignation.

Lewis said that the board’s decision has the backing of the Minister responsible for PPL's Operations Richard Maru and Kumul Consolidated Holdings Ltd, but it is yet to be accepted and formally approved by the National Executive Council, before Mr. Mobiha assumes office.

The board has also resolved to appoint Tony Koiri, as the interim Officer in Charge, whilst awaiting NEC approval for Mobiha’s appointment.

Meantime, with the impact of El-Nino, and other related issues, Mr. Lewis is urging the PPL management and employees of to work together to ensure continuity electricity services.

Though not stating the reason for his resignation, Bayly in a farewell message highlighted some of the key achievements over the last 18-months.

This includes the Commissioning of the 132 KVA line from Tari to Lae, Commissioning of Rouna 1 and refurbishment of Rouna 3, Reducing of technical and non-technical losses from about 28-percent to about 20- percent and achieving a profit in June, a first in over ten years among others.

item.title: 154 screened in Morobe breast cancer awareness drive
item.description: A breast cancer awareness programme in Morobe has screened 154 people and referred eight for further assessment, bringing important health information and screening services closer to communities in Wau and Bulolo. item.content:encoded:
A breast cancer awareness programme in Morobe has screened 154 people and referred eight for further assessment, bringing important health information and screening services closer to communities in Wau and Bulolo.

The month-long Pinktober program, led by Harmony Gold’s Hidden Valley Mine in partnership with Angau Memorial Hospital’s medical team and the PNG Cancer Relief Society, reached more than 500 community members across seven sites and surrounding communities.

Of the 154 people screened, 147 were women and seven were men. Eight people were referred for further assessment and specialist breast screening at the National Cancer Services Clinic at Angau Memorial Hospital.

The referrals highlight the importance of screening and follow-up care in helping people access further medical assessment when concerns are identified.

Throughout October, health teams provided information on breast cancer symptoms, early detection, treatment options and regular health checks. The sessions also addressed common misconceptions about the disease and raised awareness of other cancers, including mouth and cervical cancer.

For women and families in rural communities, access to accurate health information can help them recognise warning signs and seek medical attention earlier.

Harmony’s Supervisor for the Gender Development Program, Sheenie Kapen, said partnerships were important in bringing health awareness to rural and remote communities.

"Harmony is proud to partner with Angau Medical Team and the PNG Cancer Relief Society to bring this important awareness program directly to our communities. By increasing awareness and encouraging early detection, we hope to empower women, families, and communities to take proactive steps towards better health."

To support patients beyond the awareness sessions, Harmony and the Angau Cancer Clinic have also established a breast cancer referral registry to track and monitor people referred through the programme and support their follow-up care.

The registry is intended to strengthen continuity of care and help referred patients access specialist medical services.

The programme has brought screening services and cancer awareness to communities around Wau and Bulolo, with organisers encouraging people to seek health advice and participate in screening opportunities when available.

item.title: Lawyer challenges evidence against twenty-eight Sambio defendants
item.description: The defence for twenty-eight people charged over a deadly fight at Sambio village in Bulolo District has challenged the police case, arguing that key elements of the alleged offences have not been properly established. Lawyer Anthony Karahure of Makeu Legal Services has asked the Lae District Court to strike out or dismiss the charges, citing alleged defects in the wording of the charges, the iden
item.content:encoded:
The defence for twenty-eight people charged over a deadly fight at Sambio village in Bulolo District has challenged the police case, arguing that key elements of the alleged offences have not been properly established.

Lawyer Anthony Karahure of Makeu Legal Services has asked the Lae District Court to strike out or dismiss the charges, citing alleged defects in the wording of the charges, the identification of the alleged offenders and delays in providing court documents.

The application was heard by District Court Magistrate Nasiling Bingtau on Monday.

The defendants were arrested following a fight at Sambio village, Mumeng, on April 26 that left 12 men dead and several houses and properties destroyed.

Twenty-three adult defendants and three juveniles face wilful murder charges, while two other adults face arson charges.

In his notice of motion, Karahure argued that police had not adequately established the alleged intentions of the defendants, identified the principal offender or offenders, or demonstrated the presence of each defendant during the killings.

He also questioned the delay in providing court files, arguing that the defendants had remained in custody for more than four months without their charges being fully explained to them.

Karahure relied on previous court decisions to support his application for the charges to be struck out or dismissed.

Magistrate Bingtau gave the prosecution time to respond to the defence submissions and reminded it that police hand-up briefs must be prepared and served on the court and defendants.

The prosecution is expected to respond when the matter returns to court on November 16. The substantive case will also be mentioned on that date.

All 28 defendants remain remanded at Buimo Prison. The court has yet to rule on the application.

item.title: Seven suspects in police custody over Bishop Leo incident
item.description: Seven suspects allegedly involved in the recent disruption and robbery at Bishop Leo Secondary School are now in police custody. Police say the seven surrendered to Nuigo Ward 13 Councillor Tednold Wali and were handed over to police yesterday afternoon.
item.content:encoded:
Seven suspects allegedly involved in the recent disruption and robbery at Bishop Leo Secondary School are now in police custody.

Police say the seven surrendered to Nuigo Ward 13 Councillor Tednold Wali and were handed over to police yesterday afternoon.

Police are continuing efforts to apprehend the remaining suspects, with 20 suspects reportedly identified in connection with the incident.

East Sepik Provincial Police Commander Superintendent Christopher Tamari has strongly condemned the incident, which affected more than 200 Grade 12 students at Bishop Leo Secondary School last Friday.

PPC Tamari warned young people against becoming involved in similar activities, saying the consequences would not be favourable.

He also commended the collaborative efforts of police personnel, Councillor Wali and the people of Nuigo community for assisting police.

item.title: Pioneers of top school leaves a monument of legacy
item.description: A monument of rich photographic history was unveiled yesterday to honor the value and strength of pioneer students and staff of Passam National School of Excellence (NSoE) in East Sepik. Representing their legacy, the monument is a symbol of discipline, excellence, and respect - the core value of Passam NSoE.
item.content:encoded:
A monument of rich photographic history was unveiled yesterday to honor the value and strength of pioneer students and staff of Passam National School of Excellence (NSoE) in East Sepik.

Representing their legacy, the monument is a symbol of discipline, excellence, and respect - the core value of Passam NSoE.

The visiting cohorts of Passam NSoE is comprised of pioneer male students of 1978, pioneer female students of 1979, the first Deputy Principal and his wife, Bob Winnet and Delma Winnet, and the first Dux of the school, Dr. Varage John Laka.

Team lead and Chairman of Passam Pioneers Karo Gamoga says they were the first Grade 11's who built the school alongside contractors.

"It's an honor to be here 48 years later", he said.

He applauded the pioneers have contributed immensely to nation building including Yangoru-Saussia MP Richard Maru.

School Principal Samson Pitiki during his welcome speech says this sentimental event is an inspiration to the attending Grade 11's of the school.

The monument was unveiled by Bob and Delma Winnet, the second parents of the pioneers of Passam National High School.

A special feature of the monument noted during the unveiling was a small room on top of the structure that holds a Bible.

It was a significant reminder of commitment to God and the country.

item.title: Raikos health facilities receive medical drugs
item.description: Two health facilities in Madang's Raikos District have become lucky recipients of medical drugs, worth K70, 000 The medicines were recently distributed to Ileg and Saidor health centres.
item.content:encoded:
Two health facilities in Madang's Raikos District have become lucky recipients of medical drugs, worth K70, 000

The medicines were recently distributed to Ileg and Saidor health centres.

Funds for the medicines were raised through this year's annual charity golf event that is usually sponsored by Kumul Minerals Holding Ltd.

The Mineral Resources Authority donated a further K100, 000 towards the charity event.

President of Madang Golf, George Ireng said fifty thousand of the K100, 000 was also used to buy medicines, whilst the other half went to the purchase of medical equipment, all of which were distributed between Ileg, Saidor and Biliau health centres.

He explained Biliau was included because it has a large catchment area and was in dire need of medicines.

Ireng added that health workers at the three facilities were overwhelmed with the donation, which they said was timely and should take them through Christmas and to the New Year.

Mr Ireng and Robert Turik, President of the Madang Country Club, travelled with the delivery team to the district about a fortnight ago, and said they were happy with the support from all sponsors towards this worthy cause.

Esther Kana, a Community Health Worker at Saidor Health Centre, said the shortage of medical drugs is a serious problem that is faced by all health facilities in Raikos District since last year, and the intervention was highly appreciated.

At Bilia, a female nursing officer said the donation was unexpected.

She revealed that the only medicine they've had at Bilia for many months was Mala 1 and no anti- biotics, not even the basic everyday drugs.

Proceeds from last year's charity golf was used to assist Gaubin Rural Hospital on Karkar Island.

item.title: PNG Fire Service deploys firefighters to combat Manus bushfire
item.description: ​The PNG Fire Service has deployed a team of twenty firefighters today from Port Moresby to Lou Island, Manus Province, to assist local communities in responding to an escalating bushfire that threatens homes, local infrastructure, and vital food gardens.
